To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the temporal signature of translating human activity can be reliably extracted from standard PTZ camera data, (2) the temporal signature can be efficiently extracted using an original, iterative candidacy-classification reduction algorithm, and (3) the temporal signature provides a reliable, efficient, and effective means for automatically constructing a focus-of-attention scene-specific model that can be used for adaptive camera scanning.

we propose and demonstrate an efficient, adaptive, and scene-specific model that maximizes a PTZ camera's opportunity of observing human targets in its field of view, and four algorithms that exploit the adaptive, focus-ofattention model to scan a PTZ camera across its viewable field.

(a) the adaptive, focus-ofattention model is built by first detecting local motion at discrete locations across the entire viewable field, and (b) four new, effective and efficient scanning algorithms are proposed to exploit this adaptive, focus-of-at- tention model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of an adaptive model to maximize the observation of human activity in video surveillance systems.
developing a novel, adaptive, focus-of attention, model for a PTZ camera that maximizes the camera’s ability to detect humans and other moving targets.
building an adaptive, scene-specific model of human activity for a PTZ camera.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is the first to provide a PTZ camera with an adaptive focus-of-attentive model for video surveillance.

the proposed approach is an effective and efficient method for automatically constructing a focus-of-attention (FOA) model using standard PTz camera hardware, and for using that model to maximize the opportunity to observe human activity.

we present an adaptive, scene-specific model that can be used in the design and implementation of efficient, effective, and intelligent camera scanning algorithms for video surveillance and other applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a complete solution to the problem of automatic PTZ camera scanning, which is a key component for many video surveillance and monitoring systems.
we provide a new framework for the design of intelligent PTZ camera control algorithms.
we have developed a novel and efficient method for constructing an adaptive focus-of- attention model for a PTZ camera.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can automatically and adaptively construct a focus-of-attention scene-specific model using only standard PTZ camera systems.
the construction and exploitation of an activity map is a useful tool in PTZ camera scanning.
the use of a PTZ camera with a scene-specific adaptive model provides an efficient means to maximize the opportunity for detecting human activity within the overall camera field of view.
